claim: The proof of `commutator_sup_left` goes a long way round. It needs a private primed helper `commutator_sup_left'` that works in the quotient by `⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆`, and then moves everything into `M := H ⊔ K ⊔ N` through `subgroupOf`, two `map_subtype_inj` simp transfers and a `convert`. That is about 30 lines. A direct elementwise argument is shorter and needs no helper. The key facts are that `H ⊔ K` normalizes `L := ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆` (which the PR already proves) and that `commutatorElement_mul_left_eq_conj_mul` and `commutatorElement_inv_left` already exist in this file.
requested_change:
Delete the private `commutator_sup_left'`, and prove the `≤` direction directly by `commutator_le` plus `closure_induction` on `H ⊔ K = closure (H ∪ K)`, using that `H ⊔ K ≤ normalizer L`:
@[to_additive]
theorem commutator_sup_left (H K N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ := by
  refine le_antisymm (commutator_le.mpr fun g hg n hn ↦ ?_)
    (sup_le (commutator_mono_left le_sup_left) (commutator_mono_left le_sup_right))
  set L := ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆
  have hL : L ≤ N := sup_le (commutator_le_right H N) (commutator_le_right K N)
  have hHK : closure ((H : Set G) ∪ K) ≤ normalizer (L : Set G) := by
    rw [← sup_eq_closure]
    exact sup_le
      (le_normalizer_iff_commutator_le_right.mpr <| (commutator_mono_right hL).trans le_sup_left)
      (le_normalizer_iff_commutator_le_right.mpr <| (commutator_mono_right hL).trans le_sup_right)
  rw [sup_eq_closure] at hg
  induction hg using closure_induction with
  | mem x hx =>
    exact hx.elim (fun hx ↦ mem_sup_left (commutator_mem_commutator hx hn))
      (fun hx ↦ mem_sup_right (commutator_mem_commutator hx hn))
  | one => simp
  | mul x y hx _ ihx ihy =>
    rw [commutatorElement_mul_left_eq_conj_mul]
    exact mul_mem ((mem_normalizer_iff.mp (hHK hx) _).mp ihy) ihx
  | inv x hx ih =>
    rw [commutatorElement_inv_left]
    exact (mem_normalizer_iff''.mp (hHK hx) _).mp (by simpa using inv_mem ih)

@[to_additive]
theorem commutator_sup_right (N H K : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅N, H ⊔ K⁆ = ⁅N, H⁆ ⊔ ⁅N, K⁆ := by
  simp_rw [commutator_comm N, commutator_sup_left]
